Rashi on Chullin 77b:10:1.hebrew: מין בהמה חיה ועוף - ורבנן היא, דאמרי במסכת נדה (דף כא.): כל שאין בו מצורת אדם, אינו ולד:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:10:1.english: A type of domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird - And [this baraita] follows the Rabbis, who say in Tractate Niddah (21a): "Anything that does not have [something] of a human form is not [considered] a fetus":

Rashi on Chullin 77b:10:2.hebrew: אין חוששין לולד אחר - ואם נפתח הקבר בלא דם, דהואי לידה יבישתא, טהורה:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:10:2.english: There is no concern for another fetus - And if the womb opened without blood, [such] that it was a dry birth, she is [ritually] pure:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:10:3.english: [If] it is not attached to them, I impose - upon this woman:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:10:4.hebrew: חומר שתי ולדות - דחוששין שמא היה בשליא זו ולד גמור נקבה, ותשב עליו לנקבה; ואפי' בלידה יבישתא, טמאה שבועים כדין נקבה, מחמת ספק ולד אחר. וגם חומרו של זה נטיל עליה, ונאמר: ולד זה משליא זו, ולא היה בה ולד אחר, וזו אינה ולד, ואין לה שום ימי טוהר. והיינו חומר, שאם לא נמצא זה עמה, קיי"ל במסכת נדה (דף כד:): "המפלת שליא תשב לזכר ולנקבה", ונותנין לה מיהא ימי טוהר של זכר, דאין שליא בלא ולד; אבל לזו, אין ימי טהרה:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:10:4.english: The severity of two births - For we are concerned that perhaps there was in this placenta a fully formed female fetus, so she must observe [the impurity period] for a female; and even in a dry birth [without bleeding], she is impure for two weeks in accordance with the law of a female, due to the doubt of another fetus. And we also impose upon her the stringency of this [fetus], and we say: this fetus is from this placenta, and there was no other fetus in it, and this [fetus] is not a [valid] offspring, so she has no days of purity at all. And this is the stringency: for if this [fetus] were not found with it, we hold in Tractate Niddah (24b): "One who expels a placenta must observe [the stringencies] for a male and for a female," and we grant her at least the days of purity of a male, because there is no placenta without a fetus; whereas for this woman, there are no days of purity:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:11:1.english: Perhaps the fetus of this placenta dissolved - and it was a fully formed fetus:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:11:2.english: And perhaps the placenta of this fetus dissolved - [meaning] this placenta was not its [own]. Thus, we distinguish between [a placenta that is] attached and [one that is] not attached.

Rashi on Chullin 77b:12:1.hebrew: מ"ט - ישליכנה לכלבים, ולא מספקינן לה בשלית הבכור:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:12:1.english: What is the reason - [that] one may cast it to the dogs, and we do not treat it as a doubtful firstborn's placenta:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:12:2.english: Something that is consecrated with firstborn status - if it were a male:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:12:3.hebrew: נדמה - קונטרפייט"א. רחל שילדה מין עז, או עז שילדה דומה לרחל, ואמרינן בבכורות (דף יב.) דלא קדיש, דכתיב "אך בכור שור" — עד שיהא הוא שור ובכורו שור:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:12:3.english: [An animal that] resembles [another species] - Contrefaite [Old French: altered in form]. [For example,] a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like [offspring], or a goat that gave birth to [an offspring] resembling a sheep; and we say in Bekhorot (12a) that it is not consecrated [with firstborn sanctity], as it is written: "But the firstborn of an ox" — [meaning it is not consecrated] unless it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:13:1.hebrew: וכל היולדות דרכן לילד מחצה זכרים ומחצה נקבות - הלכך ולד זה ספק זכר ספק נקבה, ונקבה לא קדשה; ואת"ל זכר הוא, שמא נדמה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:13:1.english: And all [animals] that give birth tend to give birth to half males and half females - Therefore, this offspring is [a matter of] doubt [whether it is] male [or] female, and a female does not become consecrated [with firstborn status]; and even if you say it is a male, perhaps it is a nidmeh [an offspring that resembles another species]:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:13:2.english: Males become a minority - and we are not concerned about a minority:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:14:1.hebrew: רובא בר מיקדש הוא - בין זכר ובין נקבה, חוץ מנדמה:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:14:1.english: The majority is fit to be sacred - whether male or female, except for a nidmeh [an offspring that resembles a different species]:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:15:1.english: Has [an element of] healing in it - Such as a potion, or a medicine, or an incantation that one whispers over the wound:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:15:2.hebrew: אין בו משום רפואה - כגון שעושין שלא על החולי, כגון קבורת שליא בפרשת דרכים וכיוצא בהם, שדומין לניחוש:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:15:2.english: It has no medicinal [purpose] - such as [things] that they perform not for an illness, such as burying an afterbirth at a crossroads and similar things, which resemble divination:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:1:1.english: With regard to the ritual impurity of animal carcasses - whether it becomes meat, to be considered like the carcass of the donkey itself:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:4:1.hebrew: לא נצרכה - למעוטינהו, דהא ודאי לאו בשר נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:4:1.english: It is not necessary - to exclude them, for they are certainly not meat:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:4:2.english: Rather, that it was made [into] tzikei kedera - He cooked them extensively with spices:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:5:1.hebrew: לעולם לטומאת אוכלין - ומתני' לא איפשיט, דהתם "עור ששלקו" תניא, ובעור בהמה אחרת קמיירי, אבל עור חמור מאיס:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:5:1.english: Actually, [his inquiry was] regarding the impurity of foods - and it was not resolved [from] the baraita, for there it teaches "hide that one cooked," and it is speaking of the hide of another animal, whereas donkey hide is repulsive:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:6:1.english: Only where there is no fetus with it - In that [part of the placenta] that is inside [the womb]:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:6:2.english: But [if] there is a fetus with it - and we see its head and the majority of it inside [the womb]:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:6:3.hebrew: אין חוששין - שמא עוד היה ולד אחר עם זה ויצא, ושליא זו שלו היא, וזה שבפנים כבר יצתה שליתו; ומ"מ שליא זו אסורה, דשמא של ולד אחר היתה:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:6:3.english: We are not concerned - [that] perhaps there was also another fetus with this one and it exited, and this placenta belongs to it, while [as for] this [fetus] that is inside, its placenta has already exited; and nevertheless, this placenta is prohibited, because perhaps it belonged to another fetus:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:7:1.hebrew: והאמר ר' ירמיה לחומרא אמרה ר' אלעזר - דבר זה שהיה מחמיר מר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:7:1.english: And didn't Rabbi Yirmeya say: Rabbi Elazar stated it as a stringency - [Referring to] this matter, in which he [Rabbi Elazar] ruled more stringently than Rabbi Yochanan:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:8:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דאסורה באכילה, דמשמע אפילו יש עמה ולד בפנים:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:8:1.english: They only taught - that [the placenta] is forbidden to be eaten, which implies [that it is forbidden] even if there is a fetus with it inside [the womb]:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:8:2.hebrew: אלא שאינה קשורה בו - דהתם איכא למימר: לזה שבפנים היתה שליא אחרת ונמוחה ויצתה, ושליא זו של ולד אחר היתה ונמוח ויצא:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:8:2.english: [They taught this] only where it is not attached to it - For there, one can say [that] this [fetus] inside had another placenta, and it dissolved and exited, and this placenta belonged to another fetus, and it [that fetus] dissolved and exited:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:8:3.english: But [if] it is attached to it - certainly this placenta belonged to it, and it is permitted to be eaten:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:9:1.hebrew: ור' יוחנן אמר אנו אין לנו - שתהא אסורה באכילה:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:9:1.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: We have only - [the ruling] that it is forbidden to be eaten:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:9:2.hebrew: אלא שליא - שיצתה מקצתה ואין עמה ולד בפנים, דהתם חיישינן שמא יצא מיחוי הולד שם:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:9:2.english: Only a placenta - that partially emerged and there is no fetus with it inside [the womb], for there we are concerned lest the dissolved [remains of] the fetus emerged there:

Rashi on Chullin 77b:9:3.hebrew: אבל יש עמה ולד - אפי' אינה קשורה בו, מותרת, דבדידיה תלינן לה:
Rashi on Chullin 77b:9:3.english: But [if] there is a fetus with it - Even if it [the placenta] is not attached to it, it is permitted, for we attribute it to that [fetus]:

Tosafot on Chullin 77b:10:1.hebrew: המפלת מין בהמה וחיה - לא הוי מצי למינקט נפל, משום דתוך שלשה תולין בו את השליא, כדאמר רבא בפ' המפלת (נדה דף כו:):
Tosafot on Chullin 77b:10:1.english: She who expels a type of domesticated animal or undomesticated animal - [The baraita] could not have stated [the case of] a miscarried fetus, because within three [days] we attribute the placenta to it, as Rava says in the chapter [entitled] HaMapelet (Niddah 26b):

Tosafot on Chullin 77b:10:2.hebrew: הריני מטיל עליה חומר ב' ולדות - בקונטרס פי' דאתא כרבנן. אבל מתוך הלשון ד"חומר שני ולדות" משמע כר"מ דחשיב ולדות בהמה חיה ועוף, וכגון דהך בהמה הויא זכר, דאי הויא נקבה לא נפקא מינה מידי בחששא של שליא, אם לא היכא דחד קודם שקיעת החמה וחד לאחר שקיעה, כדאמרינן גבי סנדל בפרק המפלת (נדה דף כה:). אי נמי י"ל דאתיא מתני' כרבנן דלא חשבינא ליה ולד, וחומר שני ולדות הוי משום שליא גופה ולא משום בהמה, ונותנין לה חומר זכר ונקבה. ומיהו אי כרבנן אתיא, הוה ליה למימר "תשב לזכר ולנקבה ולנדה", דשמא אין כאן ולד אחד! ולפירוש הקונטרס אתי שפיר הא דלא קאמר "ולנדה", דהיינו "חומר שני ולדות" דקאמר. וא"ת: לפי מה שפירש דנקט בהמה וחיה דוקא, אבל הפילה נפל לא חיישינן לולד אחר כיון דילדה כי אורחא — הא מתני' ילדה כי אורחא וחיישינן באינה קשורה לולד אחר! ומאי סייעתא מייתי לר' אלעזר? אדרבה, קשיא ליה מהך ברייתא דנקט חיה ועוף דווקא, וסייעתא לר' יוחנן! וי"ל דאין הדבר תלוי ב"כי אורחיה", אלא פשיטא ליה למסדר הש"ס דבצורת האדם תלוי הטעם, שרגילה שליתה להתעכב; אבל אחר בהמה וחיה ועוף, לא שנא במעי אשה ולא שנא במעי בהמה, אין השליא רגילה להפרד מן הולד, אפי' ילדה הבהמה בר קיימא. וא"ת: דהכא קתני "שמא נימוח", משמע דספקא הוא; וא"כ אמאי אסורה השליא באכילה כשיצתה מקצתה ויש עמה ולד? והא ספק ספיקא הוא: שמא אין כאן ולד אחר, ואפי' את"ל יש כאן, שמא אין באותו מקצת רובא ולד! ובספ"ק דבבא קמא (דף יא.) משמע דבספק ספקא שרי, דדייקינן מיניה דאין מקצת שליא בלא ולד, הא יש מקצת שליא בלא ולד הוה ליה למשרי מספק ספיקא! וי"ל דבברייתא דקתני "שמא", היינו בשליא הבאה אחר הולד, ולעיל איירי בשליא הבאה קודם ולד; אי נמי, אסורה באכילה משום דגזרינן מקצתה אטו רובא, כדמסיק בב"ק:
Tosafot on Chullin 77b:10:2.english: I impose upon her the stringency of two births - In the Kuntres [Rashi] explained that [this baraita] accords with the Rabbis. However, from the wording "the stringency of two births," it implies [that it accords] with Rabbi Meir, who considers [fetuses in the form of] a domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird to be [valid] births; and [this applies in a case] such as where that animal [fetus] is a male, for if it were a female, there would be no practical difference at all in the concern for the placenta, except where one [was expelled] before sunset and one after sunset, as [the Gemara] states regarding a sandal [a flat, deformed fetus] in the chapter [entitled] Hamappelet (Niddah 25b). Alternatively, one can say that the baraita accords with the Rabbis, [according to whom] we do not consider it a [valid] birth, and "the stringency of two births" is on account of the placenta itself and not on account of the animal [fetus], and we impose upon her the stringency of [both] a male and a female. However, if it accords with the Rabbis, it should have said, "she must observe [the laws] for a male, and for a female, and for a niddah," since perhaps there is not even one [human] birth here! And according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], that which it does not say "and for a niddah" is well accounted for, for that is [what is meant by] "the stringency of two births" that it says. And if you ask: According to what [Rashi] explained — that [the baraita] specified a domesticated animal and an undomesticated animal specifically, whereas if she expelled a [normal] non-viable fetus we are not concerned for another fetus since she gave birth in the normal manner — behold, [in] our Mishnah [the animal] gave birth in the normal manner, yet when [the placenta] is not attached we are concerned for another fetus! And what support does [the Gemara] bring [from this baraita] for Rabbi Elazar? On the contrary, there is a difficulty against him from this baraita, which specified an undomesticated animal and a bird specifically, and [thus] it is a support for Rabbi Yochanan! And one can answer that the matter does not depend on "in its normal manner"; rather, it is obvious to the redactor of the Talmud that the reason depends on the human form, for its placenta is accustomed to remain behind; whereas after a domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird — whether in a woman's womb or in an animal's womb — the placenta is not accustomed to separate from the fetus, even if the animal gave birth to a viable [offspring]. And if you ask: Here [in the baraita] it teaches "perhaps it dissolved," which implies that it is [merely] a doubt; and if so, why is the placenta forbidden for consumption when part of it emerged and there is a fetus with it? Behold, it is a double doubt: perhaps there is no other fetus here, and even if you say there is [another fetus] here, perhaps there is not a majority of a fetus in that [emerged] part! And at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma (11a) it is implied that in [a case of] a double doubt it is permitted, for we infer from it that there is no part of a placenta without a fetus — [implying that] if there were part of a placenta without a fetus, it would be permitted because of a double doubt! And one can answer that in the baraita, which teaches "perhaps," that is [referring] to a placenta that comes after the fetus, whereas above [in our Mishnah] it is speaking of a placenta that comes before the fetus; alternatively, it is forbidden for consumption because we decree [prohibiting] a part of it on account of a majority of it, as [the Gemara] concludes in Bava Kamma:

Tosafot on Chullin 77b:13:1.hebrew: סמוך מיעוטא דנדמה למחצה דנקבות כו' - והא דתנן בפ"ג דבכורות (דף כא:): בהמה גסה ששפעה חררת דם הרי זה תקבר ונפטרה מן הבכורה, ולא אמרינן ישליכנה לכלבים מהאי טעמא דהכא — דהתם לא אמרינן תקבר אלא כדי לפרסם דנפטרה מן הבכורה, כדאמר התם. ומה שאין דוחה לומר שם כן אלא משום קושיא דפריך אר' חייא, דאמר: וכי מאחר דאינה מטמאה במגע ובמשא, אמאי תקבר? ומשני: כדי לפרסמה כו'. בלאו הכי נמי היה צריך לטעם פרסום, אלא דאדרבי חייא לא ניחא ליה כל כך שתקבר מטעם פרסום, כיון דאפילו ילדה דבר הקדוש לא בעי קבורה, משום דבטל:
Tosafot on Chullin 77b:13:1.english: Combine the minority of [animals] that resemble [another species] with the half that are females, etc. - And as for that which we learned in a Mishnah in the third chapter of Bekhorot (21b): "[With regard to] a large [domesticated] animal that discharged a clot of blood, it must be buried, and [the animal] is exempt from the [law of the] firstborn," and we do not say "he may cast it to the dogs" for this reason [given] here — [this is] because there, we only say "it must be buried" in order to publicize that [the animal] is exempt from the [law of the] firstborn, as [the Gemara] says there. And as for the fact that [the Gemara] there only offers this answer in response to the difficulty raised against Rabbi Ḥiyya, who says: "Since it does not convey impurity through contact or through carrying, why must it be buried?" and [the Gemara] answers: "In order to publicize it, etc." — even without this, [the Mishnah] would also need the reason of publicizing; it is just that against Rabbi Ḥiyya, it is not so satisfactory that it should be buried for the sake of publicizing, since even if she gave birth to something consecrated, it does not require burial, because it is nullified:

Tosafot on Chullin 77b:14:1.hebrew: רובא בר מיקדש הוא - משום דאיכא נדמה דלא קדיש, קאמר "רובא" ולא "כולה". וא"ת: והא בולד קדשים הכל קדוש, כדמוכח בתמורה בסוף פרק (כל הקרבנות) (דף יז.), דקאמר: "אבל כלאים, טומטום ואנדרוגינוס אי אתה מוצא אלא בולדות קדשים", אלמא כלאים הנולד מבהמה קדושה קדיש, וכ"ש נדמה, כדמוכח במרובה (ב"ק עח.), דקאמר: "השתא כלאים מרבה ליה, נדמה מבעיא?" וי"ל: דסוגיא דהתם כמאן דאמר ולדות קדשים במעי אמן הן קדושים, והכא למאן דאמר בהויתן הן קדושים; והא דנפל קדוש הכא, היינו משום דילפינן מבכור דקדוש בבכורה, כדדרשינן בכריתות מדכתיב "שגר". אי נמי: אפילו למאן דאמר במעי אמן הן קדושים, נקט הכא "רובא" משום דאיכא דמות דיונה דלא קדיש [וע' היטב תוספות זבחים פד: בד"ה "ומוציא", ועוד שם קיד. סד"ה "וקסבר"]:
Tosafot on Chullin 77b:14:1.english: The majority are fit to be sacred - Because there is [the case of] a nidmeh [an animal resembling a different species], which does not become sacred, [the Gemara] says "the majority" and not "all of it." And if you ask: Surely regarding the offspring of consecrated animals, everything is sacred, as is proven in Temurah at the end of the chapter [entitled] Kol HaKorbanot (17a), where it says: "However, a hybrid, a tumtum, and an androginos you find only among the offspring of consecrated animals" — thus a hybrid born from a consecrated animal is sacred, and all the more so a nidmeh, as is proven in [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 78a), where it says: "Now that it includes a hybrid, is [there any] question regarding a nidmeh?" One can answer: That sugya there follows the one who says that the offspring of consecrated animals become sacred in their mother's womb, whereas here [our Gemara] follows the one who says that they become sacred upon coming into being [at birth]; and [as for] the fact that a non-viable fetus is sacred here, that is because we derive it from a firstborn, which is sacred with firstborn sanctity, as we expound in Keritot from what is written, "the offspring (sheger)." Alternatively: even according to the one who says they become sacred in their mother's womb, [the Gemara] here used [the term] "the majority" because there is [the case of a fetus with] the likeness of a dove, which does not become sacred [and see carefully Tosafot, Zevachim 84b, s.v. "ve-motzi", and further there 114a, end of s.v. "ve-kasavar"]:

Tosafot on Chullin 77b:2:1.hebrew: עור ששלקו מטמא טומאת אוכלין - וא"ת, א"כ יאכל עור בפסח, דהא תנן (פסחים דף פד.): כל הנאכל בשור גדול בשלקא, נאכל בצלי בגדי הרך? וי"ל, דבעינן שיהא נאכל בשלקא שלא ע"י הדחק:
Tosafot on Chullin 77b:2:1.english: A hide that one cooked can become impure with the ritual impurity of foods - And if you ask: if so, let hide be eaten on Passover [as part of the paschal offering], for did we not learn (Pesachim 84a): "Whatever is eaten in a full-grown ox when boiled is eaten roasted in a tender kid"? One can answer that we require that it be eaten when boiled without difficulty:

Tosafot on Chullin 77b:3:1.hebrew: בנבלתה ולא בעור ולא בעצמות - וא"ת, אמאי לא מייתי מתני' דהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין קיז:), דתנן בהדיא דהעור אינו מצטרף לטמא טומאת נבלות? וי"ל דמייתי מהכא משום דרבה בר רב חנא קאמר עלה: "לא נצרכה אלא עשאן לציקי קדרה"; דאמתני' לא מצי למימר, דמתני' איצטריך לאשמועינן משום צירוף, דאין מצטרפין:
Tosafot on Chullin 77b:3:1.english: “Its carcass” — and not its hide, and not its bones - And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not bring the Mishnah of *HaOr VeHaRotev* (below, Chullin 117b), where we explicitly learned that the hide does not combine to impart the impurity of animal carcasses? One can answer that it brings [the proof] from here because Rabba bar Rav Ḥana says upon it: “It is necessary only [where] he prepared them as a meat pudding [tzikei kedera]”; for regarding the Mishnah [he] could not say [this], since the Mishnah was needed to teach us regarding combining — that they do not combine:

Tosafot on Chullin 77b:3:2.hebrew: ולא בעור - כשאין עליו כזית בשר, דהכי אמר בהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין קכו:), והתם נמי דרשינן "בנבלתה" — ולא בקולית סתומה, ושקולין הן:
Tosafot on Chullin 77b:3:2.english: And not its hide - [This applies] when there is not an olive's bulk of flesh upon it, for so it says in [the chapter entitled] Ha'Or VeHaRotev (later, Chullin 126b), and there too we expound: "its carcass" — and not a sealed thigh bone, and they are equal [in their derivation]:
